title: Meta's India and Southeast Asia VP Sandhya Devanathan Joins OpenAI to Lead Regional Expansion
excerpt: The Indian-origin executive will oversee consumer growth, enterprise adoption, and regulatory engagement across Southeast Asia and Australia as OpenAI races to scale its Asia-Pacific presence
body:
• Sandhya Devanathan, Meta's vice president for India and Southeast Asia, is leaving the company after more than a decade to join OpenAI as VP for Southeast Asia and Australia, starting in October.
  • Devanathan will be based in Singapore and report to Kiran Mani, OpenAI's Asia-Pacific managing director, overseeing consumer growth, enterprise adoption, partnerships, and regulatory engagement.
  • Her departure comes amid mounting regulatory scrutiny of Meta in India, including a controversy over Instagram restricting a post by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
  • OpenAI has opened offices across Asia Pacific in the past two years and recently hired former Uber India head Prabhjeet Singh to lead its India operations.

Sandhya Devanathan, one of Meta's most senior executives in Asia, is leaving the social media giant to join OpenAI in a newly created role overseeing Southeast Asia and Australia, the ChatGPT maker confirmed on Friday.

Devanathan will become OpenAI's senior-most leader in the region, taking charge of consumer growth, enterprise adoption, strategic partnerships, regulatory engagement, and regional operations. She will be based in Singapore and report to Kiran Mani, OpenAI's managing director for Asia Pacific.

A Decade at Meta

Devanathan joined Meta in 2016 when its Singapore office had roughly 300 employees. Over the following decade, she held leadership roles across the company's e-commerce and gaming businesses in Asia Pacific before being appointed vice president for India in January 2023, succeeding Ajit Mohan. She later took on responsibility for Southeast Asia as well.

"OpenAI's Asia Pacific Push The appointment underscores OpenAI's aggressive expansion across Asia Pacific, a region home to more than 600 million people."

In a LinkedIn post on Friday, Devanathan described her departure as "bittersweet," citing initiatives she led including WhatsApp-based government citizen services in India, small business storefronts across Vietnam, Indonesia, and Thailand, and startup growth across Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines.

OpenAI's Asia Pacific Push

The appointment underscores OpenAI's aggressive expansion across Asia Pacific, a region home to more than 600 million people. The company has opened offices in Singapore, Tokyo, Seoul, Sydney, and Delhi over the past two years and has been building a dedicated regional leadership team.

Indonesia and the Philippines rank among OpenAI's top 10 markets globally by ChatGPT users, making the region a critical growth frontier in the company's race against rivals including Anthropic and Google.

Devanathan's hiring follows the recent appointment of Prabhjeet Singh, who spent more than a decade at Uber leading its India and South Asia business, as OpenAI's India head. Together, the two executives give OpenAI seasoned operators with deep enterprise and government relationships across Asia's fastest-growing markets.

Meta Faces Indian Scrutiny

Devanathan's exit comes during a difficult period for Meta in India, one of its largest markets. Earlier this month, the company apologized after Instagram mistakenly restricted a post by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in July. The Indian government summoned Meta executives, including chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan, over the incident.

Following Devanathan's departure, Meta's India managing director Arun Srinivas will report directly to Benjamin Joe, the company's vice president for Asia Pacific, according to people familiar with the revised reporting structure.

Devanathan said she plans to take a short break before starting at OpenAI in October.
